definition: The streaming-native ASR architecture combining an audio encoder, a text prediction network, and a joiner that emits tokens as audio arrives.
details: The streaming-native ASR architecture combining an audio encoder, a text prediction network, and a joiner that emits tokens as audio arrives. The industry standard for on-device and live ASR (keyboards, assistants, captions) because it needs no future context.

explainer.lead: RNN-T is a streaming-native ASR architecture combining an audio encoder, a text prediction network, and a joiner that emits tokens as audio arrives. It is the industry standard for on-device and live ASR because it needs no future context.

tiers.eli5: Like a stenographer who types words the moment they hear them, without waiting for the speaker to finish the sentence.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers deploy it for live transcription where latency matters, since the joiner emits tokens as audio streams in. Its key property is that it does not require future context.
tiers.paperLevel: Three components — an audio encoder, a text prediction network, and a joiner — emitting tokens as audio arrives; streaming-native, requiring no future context.

explainer.example: A phone keyboard transcribes speech token by token as the user talks, using the joiner to emit each token without waiting for the utterance to end.
